title: Affine complete intersections admit smoothings of the expected fibre dimension
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $0\leq c\leq N$ be integers, and let $f_1,\ldots,f_c\in k[x_1,\ldots,x_N]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Suppose $P=k[x_1,\ldots,x_N]/(f_1,\ldots,f_c)\neq0$ and $\dim P=N-c=r$, so that $P$ is a global complete intersection over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. Set $R=k[[t]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] and $K=R[1/t]=k((t))$. There exist $a_{ij}\in tR$, for $0\leq i\leq N$ and $1\leq j\leq c$, such that, with $g_j=f_j+a_{0j}+\sum_{i=1}^N a_{ij}x_i$ and $Q=R[x_1,\ldots,x_N]/(g_1,\ldots,g_c)$, the map $R\to Q$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], the induced $k$-algebra map $Q/tQ\to P$ sending $x_i$ to $x_i$ is an isomorphism, and $\operatorname{Spec}(Q[1/t])\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Moreover every nonempty geometric fibre [def-weil-geometric-fibre] of $\operatorname{Spec}Q\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is equidimensional of dimension $r$ [def-weil-pure-dimension]. Empty sequences of equations and perturbation coefficients are allowed.

source.place: Tag 0E7V, lemma-smoothing-affine-lci, including its displayed polynomial construction; the expected fibre-dimension property of that construction is also used explicitly in the proof of Tag 0E7X, lemma-smoothing-at-lci-point.

proof.text: Put $R=k[[t]]$ and $A=R[x_1,\ldots,x_N]$. The field $k$ is Noetherian because its only ideals are $0$ and $k$. The power-series Noetherian theorem makes $R$ Noetherian, and the finite-type theorem makes $A$ Noetherian. The power-series domain and local-ring results give that $R$ is a domain with maximal ideal $(t)$: zero constant coefficient means exactly divisibility by $t$. More explicitly, every nonzero series is $t^d u$ for its least nonzero coefficient index $d$, with $u$ a unit. Thus every nonzero prime of $R$ contains $t$, so its only primes are $(0)$ and $(t)$. Inverting $t$ inverts every nonzero series, and hence $R_{(0)}=R[1/t]=K$ is a field, while $R_{(t)}=R$.

source.place: Tag 0E7V, lemma-smoothing-affine-lci, flatness paragraph; algebra.tex Tags 0306, 00FN and elementary lowest-coefficient factorization

proof.text: Apply the generic perturbation result to the specified $f_j$ and obtain $H\ne0$ in the $M=c(N+1)$ coefficient variables. Its conclusion holds also when $c=0$, with $M=0$ and $H=1$. This input imposes no smoothness or perfectness hypothesis on $k$ or the special fibre.

source.place: Tag 0E7V, last paragraph, invoking Tag 0E7U, lemma-jouanolou-type-thing

proof.text: Choose the coefficients explicitly. If $M=0$ the tuple is empty and $H$ is a nonzero scalar. Otherwise enumerate its variables $z_1,\ldots,z_M$ and choose an integer $D\ge2$ larger than every exponent in every monomial of $H$. Set $a_\ell=t^{D^{\ell-1}}\in tR$. Substitution takes the monomial $z_1^{e_1}\cdots z_M^{e_M}$ to $t^{\sum_\ell e_\ell D^{\ell-1}}$. The exponents in this finite sum are pairwise distinct by uniqueness of base-$D$ expansion, since $0\le e_\ell<D$. The nonzero coefficients of $H$ therefore cannot cancel, so $H(a)\ne0$ in $R$ and in $K$. Relabel these $a_\ell$ as $a_{ij}$. This proves the coefficient-choice exercise without requiring $k$ to be infinite.

source.place: Tag 0E7V, final exercise: no nonzero polynomial vanishes on all tuples in (t)

proof.text: Set $g_j=f_j+a_{0j}+\sum_i a_{ij}x_i$ and $Q=A/(g_1,\ldots,g_c)$. Reduction of coefficients modulo $t$ sends $g_j$ to $f_j$, so successive quotienting gives $Q/tQ=A/(t,g_1,\ldots,g_c)=k[x_1,\ldots,x_N]/(f_1,\ldots,f_c)=P$. Both directions send each $x_i$ to $x_i$ and each scalar to itself, giving exactly the required $k$-algebra isomorphism. Inverting $t$ similarly gives $Q[1/t]=K[x_1,\ldots,x_N]/(g_1,\ldots,g_c)$. Apply the perturbation result over $L=K$ with the coefficients chosen in step 3: this generic fibre is smooth and its $c\times c$ Jacobian minors generate its unit ideal.

source.place: Tag 0E7V, displayed construction and generic-fibre paragraph

proof.text: The polynomial projection $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is flat, and the affine flatness equivalence gives that $R\to A$ is a flat ring map. For a prime $\mathfrak q\subset Q$ containing $t$, let $\mathfrak q^*\subset A$ be its inverse image and let $\mathfrak p\subset k[x_1,\ldots,x_N]$ be its reduction modulo $t$. Then $\mathfrak p$ contains every $f_j$. Localizing the ambient flat map gives a flat local map $R\to A_{\mathfrak q^*}$ of Noetherian local rings: the contraction is $(t)$, $R_{(t)}=R$, and both rings are Noetherian by step 1 and the localized-flat-map theorem. The quotient $A_{\mathfrak q^*}/tA_{\mathfrak q^*}$ is $k[x_1,\ldots,x_N]_{\mathfrak p}$: reduction and localization commute by sending a fraction $u/v$ to $\bar u/\bar v$.

source.place: Tag 0E7V, flatness paragraph; algebra.tex Tag 00HT and morphisms.tex Tag 01U5

proof.text: Since $P\ne0$ has dimension $N-c$, the complete-intersection local regular-sequence theorem says that $f_1,\ldots,f_c$ is a regular sequence in $k[x_1,\ldots,x_N]_{\mathfrak p}$. These are exactly the reductions of $g_1,\ldots,g_c$ in the closed fibre of the flat local map in step 5. The Grothendieck regular-sequence lifting theorem therefore makes $A_{\mathfrak q^*}/(g_1,\ldots,g_c)$ flat over $R$. Its isomorphism to $Q_{\mathfrak q}$ sends the class of $u/v$ to $\bar u/\bar v$. Conversely every denominator outside $\mathfrak q$ lifts to one outside $\mathfrak q^*$; the quotient relations make this inverse independent of the lift. Thus flatness holds at each prime above $(t)$. The argument includes the empty regular sequence.

source.place: Tag 0E7V, flatness paragraph, using algebra.tex Tags 00SC (lemma-lci) and 00MG (lemma-grothendieck-regular-sequence)

proof.text: If a prime $\mathfrak q\subset Q$ does not contain $t$, its contraction in $R$ is $(0)$ by step 1, and $Q_{\mathfrak q}$ is a module over the field $R_{(0)}=K$. The field-module flatness theorem makes it flat over $R_{(0)}$. Together with step 6 this verifies the localization condition at every prime of $Q$. The flat-map local criterion now gives flatness of $R\to Q$.

source.place: Tag 0E7V, flatness at primes above (0); algebra.tex Tag 00HT

proof.text: Write $B=Q[1/t]$. At each prime of $B$ some Jacobian minor $\delta$ is invertible by step 4. Permute variables so that this minor uses the first $c$ variables. The principal open $D(\delta)$ has coordinate ring $B_\delta=K[x_1,\ldots,x_N,y]/(g_1,\ldots,g_c,y\delta-1)$. For the $c+1$ derivative columns $x_1,\ldots,x_c,y$, the displayed Jacobian has upper-right block zero and bottom-right entry $\delta$; its determinant is $\delta^2$ up to the harmless permutation sign. It is a unit in $B_\delta$. Order the variables as $x_1,\ldots,x_c,y,x_{c+1},\ldots,x_N$ so these are the first $c+1$ columns. This is a standard smooth presentation with $N+1$ variables and $c+1$ equations. The standard-smooth dimension theorem gives local topological dimension $(N+1)-(c+1)=r$ at every point of this open. For a point $b$ in this principal open $U$, every open neighbourhood $V$ of $b$ in $\operatorname{Spec}B$ contains the neighbourhood $V\cap U$ of $b$ in $U$, and $\dim(V\cap U)\leq\dim V$: a chain of irreducible closed subsets of an open subset gives a chain of the same length by taking closures. Conversely each open neighbourhood of $b$ in $U$ is open in $\operatorname{Spec}B$. The two minima defining local topological dimension are therefore equal. These opens cover $\operatorname{Spec}B$, so $\dim_b\operatorname{Spec}B=r$ for every $b$. When $c=0$, use the single empty minor $\delta=1$; the same presentation and calculation apply.

source.place: Tag 00T7, lemma-standard-smooth; explicit localization chart for the full-rank minors in examples-defos.tex Tag 0E7U

proof.text: The special fibre $\operatorname{Spec}P$ has local topological dimension $r$ at every point by the global-complete-intersection equidimensionality theorem applied to the given presentation and dimension hypothesis. For any geometric point over $(t)$ with algebraically closed residue field $\Omega$, the geometric fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}(P\otimes_k\Omega)$ by the isomorphism in step 4. The pointwise field-extension dimension theorem gives local dimension $r$ at every point of it. For a geometric point over $(0)$ the fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_K\Omega)$, and the same theorem with the result of step 8 gives local dimension $r$ there. Its use is legitimate because $P$ and $B$ are finitely generated algebras over their respective fields. These are all geometric fibres since $(t)$ and $(0)$ are all primes of $R$.

Each geometric fibre has coordinate algebra finitely generated over the field $\Omega$, hence Noetherian by the finite-type Noetherian theorem. Its spectrum is locally Noetherian by the definition, using its one-member affine cover. Apply the constant-local-dimension component theorem to the whole geometric fibre and the integer $r$: step 9 supplies its local dimension hypothesis, so every irreducible component has dimension $r$. This is equidimensionality of dimension $r$ by definition. The assertion is vacuous for an empty fibre. Steps 3, 4 and 7 give all the other requested conclusions, including the prescribed coordinate identification of the special fibre.
